thread:
Maya Chen: Quick sync — follow-ups from last night's postmortem. I spun up a rough action list for runbook/playbook edits. Main themes: unclear canary escalation path, missing triage commands for cache thrash, and inconsistent owner handoffs.
Igor Petrov: Thanks. Can you paste the recurrence map you mentioned? I want to see if this pattern matches previous KV-cache incidents.
Maya Chen: Pasted the short recurrence notes below. High-level: 3 events in 6 weeks where prefix cache size spikes -> eviction -> elevated latencies -> cascade to serving pool. Each time fallback/canary logic didn't kick in reliably.
Samantha Lee: Ugh. We should add an explicit step to check canary health first, before failing over. Right now the runbook assumes canary will always be healthy.
Eli Nguyen: I can own the canary-health step. Plan: add a pre-failover check + a quick command to validate canary model responses. Due: 2026-03-27 EOD. @nate FYI for rollout coordination.
Nate R.: Ack. I'll block a 30m window to test canary checks with traffic replay.
Maya Chen: Good. For triage commands, suggested one-liners:

```
# check cache metrics for model X
curl -sS http://metrics.internal/kvcache?model=x | jq .evictions
# validate canary response
curl -sS http://canary.service/v1/predict -d '{"prompt":"ping"}' | jq .status
```

Samantha Lee: Add those to runbook under "triage commands" and mark as verified. Also add exact thresholds (evictions > 100/min) to trigger escalation.
Igor Petrov: I'll map the recurrence pattern to the timeline and attach related incident IDs to the postmortem doc. Might be a config knob causing frequent evictions.
runbook-bot: Created task RB-4382 "Add canary health precheck + triage commands" and assigned to Eli Nguyen. Due 2026-03-27.
Eli Nguyen: I'll update the runbook with the commands and a quick test checklist. Proposal for checklist items: 1) check canary status 2) inspect kvcache evictions 3) run small traffic replay 4) engage Dedicated failover if canary fails.
Maya Chen: Love it. Also add an "Escalation path" section: exact paging sequence if failover is required (oncall -> runtime lead -> infra). Right now it's vague.
Samantha Lee: Note: add runnable snippets for the failover (so oncall can copy/paste). Something like:

```
# promote canary fallback
kubectl -n inference set image deploy/serving-main serving=serving:canary
# or trigger routing policy
rbctl route swap --from canary --to stable --model x
```

Igor Petrov: I'll review the kubectl/rbctl snippets with eng-runtime to make sure they won't break autoscale.
Nate R.: We should also add a follow-up EPIC for long-term fixes (cache sizing, smarter eviction policy). I'll create EPIC-670 and link to the runbook changes.
Maya Chen: Assignments recap: Eli -> runbook edits + triage command tests (due 2026-03-27). Igor -> recurrence mapping + incident linkbacks (due 2026-03-25). Nate -> EPIC creation + rollout window (due 2026-03-28). Sam -> verify thresholds & copyedit runbook language (due 2026-03-26).
Samantha Lee: I'll also add a short "how to revert" snippet under each change. People panic during outages if they don't know how to revert quickly.
Eli Nguyen: Quick Q: do we want these changes in the main runbook repo or a guarded branch until we test? Recommend guarded branch + canary deploy of runbook changes.
Maya Chen: Guarded branch makes sense. Add a small QA checklist: dry-run in staging + one simulated eviction runbook test.
runbook-bot: Comment on RB-4382: "QA checklist added".
Maya Chen: Thanks everyone. I'll update the postmortem doc with the new action table and timeline after we confirm owners. Ping here when you've created any linked tickets. :white_check_mark:
